 Judgement
The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/s 166 of the M.V Act claiming the compensation on
account of the injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicles Accident.

The case of the petitioner is as under:
That, on 20.11.2016 at about 8.30 p.m, the petitioner was riding the Pulsar motor
cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-Y-7175 proceeding from Kantanakunte towards
Doddaballapura, slowly by observing all the traffic rules on the left side of the road,
when he reached near Amanikere Palanajogihalli village, at that time the driver of the
car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MM-1106 coming from Doddaballapura towards
Gowribidanur in high speed, rash and negligent manner, endangering human life,
came to the extreme wrong side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's motor
cycle.
Due to impact petitioner fell down and sustained injuries all over the body.

After the accident he was shifted to Nandi Hospital, Doddapallapura, wherein he took
first aid and then shifted to Prolife Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as
an inpatient from 19.11.2016 to 30.11.2016 for a period of 12 days.

During the course
of treatment he undergone surgery and implants were fixed.

He was discharged with an advice to regular follow up treatment, so far as he has spent
Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical and Rs.50,000/- towards nourishment expenses.
3 . It is alleged that at the time of accident he was doing Fabrication work, earning Rs.500/- per day.

Due to the accidental injuries, he took prolonged treatment; thereby he was unable to attend his
work and lost income.

He has suffered permanent disability and unable to walk, run, squats, lift
heavy weight, lead a normal life, as he was doing prior to the accident.

That, the accident is occurred
due to rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver, and the police have registered a case and
charge sheet came to be filed against the driver of the offending car.

Respondent No.1 and 2 being
the insurer and Rc Owner of the offending car are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation

4. After service of notice of the petition, respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared, respondent No.1 has
filed the detailed statement of objection.
Respondent No.2 has not chosen to file any objection.

5. The respondent No.1 denied all the averments made in the claim petition and called upon the
petitioner to prove the same with strict proof.

This respondent admitted the issuance of insurance
policy and its force in respect of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MM-1106 and the liability of this
respondent if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is contended that,
the driver of the car was not having valid and effective Dl to drive the same at the time of accident.

This respondent denied the involvement of the car and rash and negligent driving of the car in the
alleged accident but contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner as
he was riding his motor cycle without proper lookout vehicular movements of the road, and without
noticing oncoming vehicles he himself fall from motorcycle and sustained injuries.

The 6 Scch-24
MVC.No.971/2017 claim of the petitioner is highly excessive and prays to dismiss the petition
against 1st respondent.

6. Based on the above pleadings of the parties following issues came to be framed by this Tribunal:-
Issues
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road
traffic accident that occurred on 20.11.2016 at about 8.30 p.m, near Amanikere,
Palanajogihalli village, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru District, due
to the rash and negligent driving of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-MM-1106 by its
driver as alleged ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as claimed ?

If so, to what
amount and from whom ?
3.
What order
or Award ?

7. In order to substantiate the case made out by the petitioner, he himself examined as P.W.1 and
examined one witness as P.W.2 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.17.

Thereafter, the petitioner closed
his side evidence.

8. In order to rebut the evidence so placed on record by the petitioner, the respondents have not
chosen to examine any witness nor produced any documents.

sentences.text: After hearing the arguments this Tribunal has passed judgment and award dated 31-03-2018.

Aggrieved by the correctness of the order passed by this court, the Petitioner has preferred appeal in
M.F.A.No:6485/2019 (Mv-I) before the Hon'ble High court.

Before the Hon'ble High Court the
appellant/ petitioner contended that they have not examined the doctor before the Tribunal as such
the disability was not considered by the Tribunal and that the petitioner was admitted to the
hospital and was inpatient for a period of 10 days and he incurred medical expenses as per Ex.P12
and now the petitioner intends to examine the doctor before the Tribunal and prayed to remand the
matter back to the Tribunal.
8 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017
10.

The Hon'ble High Court by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant,
remanded the matter to the Tribunal with direction to adduce medical evidence with specific order
that Petitioner is not entitled for interest from 31-03-2018 to 07-08-2025 on any enhanced amount
by the Tribunal.

While remanding the case, direction was given to his Tribunal to dispose of the
matter within 4 weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order by providing
opportunity to both the parties and further direction was given to the parties to appear before the
Tribunal on 28-08-2025 without awaiting further notice.

11. As borne out records, the certified copy of the order passed by the Hon'ble High Court in Mfa
No. 6485/2019 was received by this court on 30-08-2025.

Since the order passed by the Hon'ble
High Court was received by this court on 30-08-2025 ie., subsequent to 9 Scch-24
MVC.No.971/2017 the date fixed by the Hon'ble High Court for the appearance of the parties
(28-08-2025) and case file was put up before this court on 06-09-2025, the court notice was issued
to the petitioner and respondent no.1 and 2 by fixing the date of appearance on 18-09-2025.

On
service of summons, respondent no.1 & 2 appeared through their counsels.

The counsel for
petitioner remained absent without any representation.

As Hon'ble High Court has given only 4
weeks time to dispose of the case, direction was given to the petitioner by this court to adduce the
medical evidence for the said purpose case case was remanded.

On 19-09-2025 the petitioner filed
Ia No.III, u/O 16 Rule 1 and 2 Cpc to issue summons to the Medical Officer.

The said application
was allowed on the said date itself and while allowing the application direction was given to the
effect

that in the adjourned date if the evidence of the Medical Officer is adduced in 10 Scch-24
MVC.No.971/2017 chief then respondents have to cross examine the witness on the said date itself
and accordingly case was adjourned till 23-09-2025.

12. On 23-09-2025 though the witness i.e., Medical Officer was present and counsel for respondent
no.2 was present, but the counsel for petitioner prayed time to lead the medical evidence.

By
considering the submission of the petitioner, case was adjourned till 24- 09-2025.

On 24-09-2025
the learned counsel for petitioner again sought for adjournment hence adjournment was granted till
26-09-2025.

On the said date also instead of keeping the witness present, the learned counsel for
petitioner prayed time without assigning any reason.

Hence prayer was rejected and Medical
evidence was taken as nil and posted the case to 27-09-2025 for addressing the argument.

On 27-09-2025, the learned counsel for respondent no.1 and 2 were present before the court but
counsel for petitioner remained absent before the court from 11-00 am., till 5-00 pm.,

Hence, with
no other option this court by hearing the arguments of respondent no.1 and 2 posted the case for
judgment.

14. After the case is remanded to this court, since the petitioner has not adduced medical evidence
the purpose for which case was remanded and there is no additional evidence placed on record by
the respective parties after the remand of case, the judgment and decree passed by this court dated
31-03-2018 holds good.
15. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials placed on record.

16. My findings on the above issues are as under:
12 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 Issue No.1 - In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 - Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 - As per final order, for the following ;

Reasons Issue No.1:
17.

In order to prove the negligence, the petitioner himself entered into witness box and filed
affidavit in lieu of examination-in-chief and got examined as P.W.1.

He reiterates the averments and
the allegations made in the petition.

During the course of cross-examination of respondent No.1 he
denied the suggestions that, he himself falls from motor cycle and the accident was not occurred by
the offending car.

18. The respondent No.1 has also denied the rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver and
contended that the accident is occurred due to negligence of the petitioner as he himself fall from
the motor cycle as 13 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 he was riding the same unmindfully, without
following the traffic rules and contributed the accident.

It is also contended that the driver of the car
was not possessing valid and effective Dl to drive the car as on the date of accident.

19. P.W.1 has relied upon various copies of police documents produced at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 i.e Fir,
Complaint, Spot mahazar, Imv report, Wound Certificate and Charge sheet.

It is pertinent to note
that, Ex.P.1, the Fir discloses that, the criminal case has been registered & after investigation, the
police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-04- Mm-1106 for
the offences punishable U/s 279, 337 of Ipc.

The police documents are marked without any
objections and prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the car.

The respondents have not made any attempt to examine the 14 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 driver
of the car to show that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the car is the best witness to say about the accident and negligence.

In the absence of
the rebuttal evidence, an adverse inference can be drawn against the respondents.

Under these
circumstances, the evidence of P.W.1, coupled with the contents of the police documents, establishes
that, the accident has caused solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver.

Accordingly, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

Pw.2, who has produced Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.17 i.e. Authorization letter, 2-Case sheets with 4-X-ray
films.

It is the case of the petitioner that, after the accident he was shifted to Nandi Hospital,
Doddaballapura, wherein he took firsts aid and then he was shifted to Prolife Hospital, wherein he
took treatment as an inpatient from 19.11.2016 to 30.11.2016 for a period of 12 days.

During the
course of cross 16 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 examination it is denied that, no accident is occurred
as on 20.11.2016 by the offending car, but Pw.1 has filed false complaint against the said car.

On this
Pw.1 deposed that, infact accident occurred on 19.11.2016 but by oversight, it is mentioned as
20.11.2016 in the complaint.

In this respect I have gone through the record specifically the
complaint alleged to be given by the father of the petitioner on 22.11.2016.

In the said complaint it is
alleged that, his son met with accident on 20.11.2016 Saturday at about 8.30 p.m. Of course date of
the accident is wrongly mentioned as occurred on 20.11.2016 but it is occurred on 19.11.2016 as per
hospital records which are prepared first in time and 19.11.2016 fallen on Saturday which is rightly
mentioned in the complaint as accident occurred on Saturday 19.11.2016.

23 . It is alleged by the petitioner that, During the course of treatment he undergone surgery and
internal fixators are fixed.

He again admitted to the above said hospital at 2nd instance from
14.12.2016 to 23.12.2016 for about 10 days.

Due to accidental injuries he has suffered pain and
mental agony.
He has spent Rs.3,50,000/- towards medicine and other incidental expenses.

In this
regard he has produced 2-Discharge summaries and 2-case sheets at Ex.P.7, 8, 16 and Ex.P.17.

The
contents of the respective medical documents makes it very clear with regard to the gravity of the
injuries sustained by the Claimant.

As per the evidence of the Claimant, he is still under treatment
and could not resume his avocation and daily activities till date.

By taking into consideration of the
duration of the treatment as Inpatient, Outpatient, continued follow up

, I am of the considered
opinion that the petitioner has 18 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 suffered severely due to the
accidental injuries.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards Pain and sufferings.

Further, it can be said that the petitioner must have incurred some

Thus, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.30,000/- towards Attendant, conveyance
and other incidental expenses.
24. It is the evidence of P.W.1 that, she has spent a sum of Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses.

In order to substantiate the said fact, he has produced 51- Prescriptions at Ex.P.12 and 30-medical
bills worth of Rs.4,75,343/- at Ex.P.13.

He deposed that, he has producing the bills worth of
Rs.4,75,343/- and some of the bills are misplaced during the hospitalization.

Taking into
consideration of the nature of the injuries and the 19 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 treatment as an
inpatient and actual medical bills, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for a sum of
Rs.4,75,343/- towards Medical Expenses.

25. The case of the petitioner is that, at the time of accident, he was aged about 31 years and was
doing Fabrication work and earning Rs.500/- per day.

Due to the accidental injuries he is
permanently disabled and unable to walk, run, squat, ride motor cycle, lift heavy weight, unable to
attend his work, thereby he sustained loss of income which is resulted in great financial hardship.

In
order to substantiate the avocation and earnings of the petitioner, he has not produced any
documents nor to show that, he has suffered loss of income during the treatment period.

The
petitioner has also not produced any documents to show that he has not attended to his work.

Except the oral evidence he has not produced any documents to prove that, he has 20 Scch-24
MVC.No.971/2017 suffered loss of earnings during the period of treatment.

Under such
circumstances, considering the age of the petitioner and the conditions prevailed at the time of
accident, I deem it just and proper to take the income of the petitioner as Rs.8,000/- p.m.

Hence, in
my opinion the accident rendered the petitioner incapable to attend his normal work at least for a
period of 3 months.

Considering the same, I award Rs.24,000/- towards Loss of income during the
period of treatment.

26. It is the evidence of P.W.1 that, inspite of best available treatment he suffered permanent
disability.

After the accident due to the injuries sustained by him, he could not be active, cannot
walk for a long distance and now unable to lead normal life as he was doing prior to the accident and
unable to do any other manual work and his day-to-day activities.

Whereas in support of his alleged
disability to carry out his day-to-day activities, he 21 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 has not made any
attempt to examine his treated doctor nor any expert / Medical officer before this Tribunal.

It is not
the evidence of P.W.1 that, the doctor has advised him not to do work.

So in the absence of any
experts' evidence & supporting documents this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not
entitled for the compensation under the head Loss of future earnings.

27. The injuries sustained by the petitioner shows that he must have sustained pain and suffering
and the accident has put him in discomfort and has lost the amenities of life to some extent.

Taking
all these facts into consideration, the petitioner is entitled for a compensation of Rs.40,000/-
towards Loss of Amenities of Life.

Thus, I am of the considered opinion that, the petitioner is
entitled for the compensation under the following heads :

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The police documents are marked without any
objections and prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
The respondents have not made any attempt to examine the 14 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 driver
of the car to show that, there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the car is the best witness to say about the accident and negligence.
In the absence of
the rebuttal evidence, an adverse inference can be drawn against the respondents.
Under these
circumstances, the evidence of P.W.1, coupled with the contents of the police documents, establishes
that, the accident has caused solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the car by its driver.
Ashok Kumar K.T vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 29 September, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195402801/
5

Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has established the rash and negligent
driving on the part of the driver of the alleged car and he has sustained injuries in the said accident.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
By taking into consideration of the
duration of the treatment as Inpatient, Outpatient, continued follow up
, I am of the considered
opinion that the petitioner has 18 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 suffered severely due to the
accidental injuries.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards Pain and sufferings.
After the accident due to the injuries sustained by him, he could not be active, cannot
walk for a long distance and now unable to lead normal life as he was doing prior to the accident and
unable to do any other manual work and his day-to-day activities.
Whereas in support of his alleged
disability to carry out his day-to-day activities, he 21 Scch-24 MVC.No.971/2017 has not made any
attempt to examine his treated doctor nor any expert / Medical officer before this Tribunal.
It is not
the evidence of P.W.1 that, the doctor has advised him not to do work.
So in the absence of any
experts' evidence & supporting documents this Tribunal is of the opinion that, the petitioner is not
entitled for the compensation under the head Loss of future earnings.
27. The injuries sustained by the petitioner shows that he must have sustained pain and suffering
and the accident has put him in discomfort and has lost the amenities of life to some extent.
